papers.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
papers.abstract: A language model is trained once and frozen. Making it better takes another training run, or a prompt, a harness or extra computation at inference that is gone once the task ends. We show a third way: to our knowledge for the first time, a language model rewrites its own weights by its own reasoning and becomes better, with no gradients and no training. We call this self-rewriting: the model is its own optimizer. In earlier work, a frontier model edited a much smaller one; here an open 27B model, given its weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself, diagnoses its own failure and rewrites the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on problems it never saw. It keeps getting better: it tests its edits on practice problems and submits only what works, each edit improving on the last, and over eight consecutive sessions its accuracy only rises. It repairs a damaged copy of itself, like a broken robot that fixes itself without being rebuilt: the copy solves almost nothing, yet with no retraining and without ever reading the original weights, the model brings it back to over 80% of the original accuracy on image tasks it never saw. And the ability emerges with scale: in one model family, the smaller models make no edit or break themselves, and only the largest improves and repairs itself. Unlike test-time scaling, self-rewriting writes its gain into the weights, at no cost per answer; unlike training, it runs only forward passes, as serving does. The wall between training and inference is a limit of our tools, not a property of intelligence. We believe self-rewriting is a necessary step toward recursive self-improvement: a model that, like a human, does not separate training from inference could keep upgrading itself for life, with no larger model, no harness or prompt engineering, and no pre- or post-training.

summary.en: Self-rewriting lets an open 27B model diagnose its failures and rewrite its own weights via forward-only reasoning, no gradients or training, gaining 6.6 points on unseen problems and restoring a damaged copy to over 80% of original accuracy.
summary.zh: 自改写方法让开放 27B 模型仅凭前向推理、无梯度无训练地诊断自身失败并重写自身权重，在未见问题上准确率提升 6.6 个百分点，连续八轮编辑精度持续上升，还能把近乎失效的受损副本恢复到原精度 80% 以上，且该能力仅在最大模型中涌现。

papers.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
papers.abstract: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges. Upstream proxies vary from coarse layouts to fine articulated geometry depending on the interaction, and streaming inference must operate in a few causal steps without accumulating drift across self-generated history. We present Invoker-Render, pairing a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model under a shared conditioning interface over structural proxies, an appearance reference, and language. Trained on an aligned approximately 200-hour multi-granularity corpus, Invoker-Render honors fine geometric constraints when supplied while synthesizing plausible local motion under coarse proxies, enabling runtime selection of input detail. To bridge bidirectional creation and real-time streaming without compounding step compression and rollout drift, we introduce Progressive Forcing (ProForcing). ProForcing first trains a causal predictor and distills it into a four-step renderer using histories derived from training videos. Training then shifts to continuous self-generated rollouts. A pipelined serving stack supports efficient streaming inference. Experiments show versatile control across proxy families, granularities, and camera paths, consistent gains over recent streaming baselines, and stable 30-minute racing rollouts that preserve scene and subject appearance.

summary.en: Invoker-Render couples a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model sharing a structural-proxy, appearance-reference and language interface; Progressive Forcing distills video-history training into self-generated rollouts, yielding stable 30-minute racing streams over streaming baselines.
summary.zh: Invoker-Render 结合双向创作模型与因果四步流式模型，统一以结构代理、外观参考和语言为条件，并用 Progressive Forcing 从视频历史蒸馏到自生成 rollout；实验在代理类型、粒度、相机路径上控制灵活，较流式基线稳定提升，支持 30 分钟赛车生成不漂移。

papers.title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Latent diffusion models rely on a decoder to map denoised latents to pixels, adding complexity and inference cost. We introduce Decoding Without a Decoder (DWD), which lets a finetuned diffusion transformer produce final pixels directly through a linear head. Unlike previous methods, where the denoising output leads to final pixels, DWD separates the two roles: the original denoising head continues to drive sampling, then the new DWD head predicts the pixels at the final step. We extend pretrained latent models with DWD efficiently by finetuning only the last few transformer blocks, training the DWD head with pixel quality losses while anchoring the denoising head to the pretrained model to preserve the sample trajectory. Across latent image and video generators, DWD removes the decoder while maintaining or even improving pixel quality. On Wan video generation, it visibly reduces detail distortion and flickering, lowering warping error by 23%. Remarkably, the same separation also improves pixel diffusion models that do not even use a decoder: a final-step DWD head produces substantially better texture detail in text-to-image generation, and improves ImageNet FID from 1.55 to 1.43, a new state of the art among pixel flow models.

summary.en: DWD lets a finetuned diffusion transformer predict final pixels via a linear head at the last sampling step, removing the decoder; it cuts Wan video warping error by 23% and improves pixel-flow ImageNet FID from 1.55 to 1.43.
summary.zh: DWD 让微调后的扩散 transformer 通过线性头在最后一步直接预测像素，替代解码器；仅微调末几个 block 并锚定去噪头，在 Wan 视频生成上降低 23% warping error，并将像素流模型的 ImageNet FID 从 1.55 降至 1.43。

papers.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
papers.abstract: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

summary.en: Posterior Matching Distillation combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation by matching exponentially tilted student sample means, achieving the best 4-step FID on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B.
summary.zh: PMD 将模式覆盖的后验采样与任意步数生成结合，通过匹配指数重加权学生样本均值来学习教师后验，在 SDXL 和 FLUX.2 [klein] 4B 上取得 4 步方法中最佳 FID。

papers.title: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
papers.abstract: Computer-using agents are increasingly expected to complete realistic user goals rather than isolated GUI actions. However, existing benchmarks typically isolate web, mobile, or desktop environments, leaving it unclear whether a single generalist agent can execute long-horizon workflows that span multiple operating systems and persistent application states. We introduce OS-Omni, a live cross-platform benchmark and execution environment for evaluating computer-using agents across Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web environments. OS-Omni is released in versioned waves of 300 tasks each; this paper focuses on the first release, v1, which contains 48 tasks per platform and 12 cross-platform workflows that pair a desktop with an Android phone. OS-Omni provides reproducible initialization, platform-specific adapters, trajectory logging, and executable final-state evaluators, and includes controlled service-backed applications for workflows involving account, cart, budget, calendar, message, and other persistent state. Human studies show that OS-Omni tasks require 67.54 interaction steps, substantially exceeding OSWorld references of 15.0 steps. On v1, the strongest evaluated agent, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches 68.5% average success, trailing the 77.3% human reference by 8.8 points; the gap is uneven across platforms, with frontier models exceeding humans on Linux but trailing them by more than 25 points on iOS and macOS. These results indicate that current agents remain far from platform-robust, long-horizon computer use, especially when success requires sustained state tracking and durable final-state changes.

summary.en: OS-Omni is a live cross-platform benchmark for computer-using agents spanning Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web; its v1 has 48 tasks per platform plus 12 cross-platform workflows averaging 67.54 steps. Claude Opus 5.5 scores 68.5% versus 77.3% human, trailing by over 25 points on iOS and macOS.
summary.zh: OS-Omni 是覆盖 Windows、Ubuntu、macOS、iOS、Android 和 Web 的跨平台计算机代理实时基准，v1 每平台 48 个任务、另含 12 个跨平台工作流，任务平均需 67.54 步；最强代理 Claude Opus 5.5 平均成功率 68.5%，低于人类 77.3%，在 iOS 和 macOS 上差距超过 25 点。
